- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); model often fails to revert; adjust forecast to align with 14–18 day moving average.
- When official events are frequent (≥15 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model overconfidently assumes stability; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to smooth out volatility; increase forecast volatility by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
